answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may vote on a bridge transaction. The contract caps each stake’s voting weight and penalizes provably conflicting signatures, so splitting funds across a thousand fresh identities does not create a thousand independent votes. To gain influence, an attacker must acquire and lock more real capital; equivocation risks losing it. A crystal-clear rule can specify the evidence and penalty, while quartz is merely a name and grants no extra credibility.
